Every file read in full: domain root unit = credits-attribution-index.md, credits-attribution-cx.md, 02.05, 02.06, 02.07, 02.08, 02.09, 02.10 (8 files); 02.01 = index, cx, 02.01.01-02.01.06 (8); 02.02 = index, cx, 02.02.01-02.02.04 (6); 02.03 = index, cx, 02.03.01-02.03.03 (5); 02.04 = index, cx, 02.04.01-02.04.04 (6). Dimensions 1 (Problem Clarity), 2 (Persona Specificity), 4 (Constraint Explicitness) and 6 (Competitive Positioning) are N/A for every unit: they are owned by meta/problem-statement.md, meta/personas.md, meta/constraints.md and meta/competitive-landscape.md, which sit outside this domain and are referenced but never redefined here (credits-attribution-index.md:70 — 'Personas from meta/personas.md — referenced, never redefined'). findings.claim: 02.10 grants the Producer session-level AI disclosure while the same file's D-04, its edge-case table and its states table forbid a Producer disclosing on anyone's contribution but their own. The two cannot both be built.
findings.evidence: 02.10-ai-contribution-disclosure.md:19 (Role Lens, Producer) — 'Full | Discloses at the session level and per contribution. The de-facto compliance point, because they assemble the record and they are who a label asks.' Contradicted by 02.10-ai-contribution-disclosure.md:122 (D-04) — 'You disclose your own contribution only | Disclosing someone else's work as AI is an assertion about their craft and is defamatory if wrong.'; by 02.10-ai-contribution-disclosure.md:71 (edge case) — 'Producer discloses AI on someone else's contribution | Not permitted — it is an assertion about how another person made their work, and if wrong it is defamatory | Own contributions only'; and by 02.10-ai-contribution-disclosure.md:86 (states) — 'Partial | Some contributions disclosed, others silent | Per-contribution, never per-record'. Reinforced from outside the file: credits-attribution-cx.md:266 (CX-14) — 'Contribution logged by Producer → AI axis defaults unset → named contributor sets/clears their own axis (async). The Producer cannot pre-fill an AI claim about the contributor.' and 02.02.02-per-track-contribution-log.md:109 — 'Producer tries to set the AI disclosure axis on someone else's contribution | Refused.' The domain Role Matrix compounds it: credits-attribution-index.md:85 gives 02.10 Producer '✅ Full' where the Musician — who owns exactly the same scope under D-04 — is '⚙️ Config (own contributions)'.
findings.forcedInvention: Whether a session-level AI disclosure control exists for the Producer at all, and if it does, whether it writes the disclosure axis onto other parties' contribution rows (which D-04 calls defamatory) or only onto the Producer's own rows. Nothing in the domain answers it, and no open question tracks it.

findings.claim: 02.08's happy path gates embargoed-credit inclusion on whether the export's RECIPIENT is a session participant, while its own edge-case row, credits-attribution-cx.md CX-10 and 02.01.05 all gate it on the export's SCOPE (participant-scoped vs catalog-scoped). Under the recipient test a musician could not export their own embargoed credit to a non-participant, which 02.01.05 D-09 forbids.
findings.evidence: 02.08-credit-export-ddex-rin.md:50 (Happy Path step 4) — 'Package generates; embargoed credits excluded unless the recipient is a participant'. Contradicted by its own edge case at 02.08-credit-export-ddex-rin.md:59 — 'Embargoed credits in scope | Excluded by default; participant-scoped export may include them'; by credits-attribution-cx.md:200 (CX-10) — 'participant-scoped export may include embargoed credits; catalog-scoped export excludes them and states the exclusion explicitly' and CX-10 Q3 at credits-attribution-cx.md:207 — 'Scope (participant vs catalog) is the permission that decides whether embargoed rows are eligible at all'; and by 02.01.05-credit-visibility-embargo.md:163 — 'a participant may export the embargoed credits of sessions they participated in, and their own credits always. A non-participant-scoped export (a Producer's whole catalog, a room's discography) excludes embargoed credits'. The recipient test also breaks the anti-weaponisation control at 02.01.05-credit-visibility-embargo.md:273 (D-09) — 'The credited party always sees and can export their own credit.'
findings.forcedInvention: Whether the embargo filter on export keys off the exporting party's participation (a fact the platform holds) or the receiving party's participation (a fact the platform generally cannot know for a downloaded file).

findings.claim: 02.01.01 renders the contested badge on the work's ledger to every viewer who can see the work, while 02.01.02, 02.05 and credits-attribution CX-16 state as an authoritative single rule that a contest is never publicly disclosed and is a participant-only record-view affordance. The work's ledger is reachable by non-participants, so the two rules produce different pages for the same viewer.
findings.evidence: 02.01.01-credit-record-contribution-ledger.md:104 (edge case, 'Party disputes a record naming them') — 'Contested badge on the work's ledger for all who can see the work.' Same file:105 — 'The contest marks; it never suppresses (D-11) | Contested badge — visible, not absent'; and same file:141 (Record Lifecycle States) — 'Contested | Dispute filed (02.05) | Contested marker on the work's ledger; zero weight in derived surfaces'. Contradicted by 02.01.02-public-discography.md:137 — 'The single winning rule, stated once: contest = a public marker on the record view for participants only; the public discography line is unchanged and never hidden.'; by 02.05-credit-dispute-resolution.md:21 (Fan Role Lens) — 'They see the unchanged public discography line; a contest marker is participant-and-credited-party record-view information, never a public disclosure'; and by credits-attribution-cx.md:292 (CX-16 role scoping) — 'Fan sees the unchanged public page (no contest state leaks)'. That the work's ledger is a non-participant surface is established by 02.01.02-public-discography.md:55 — 'Reader walks the graph: clicks a work (→ its ledger, 02.01.01, itself viewer-scoped)' and by 02.01.01-credit-record-contribution-ledger.md:151, whose Empty ledger state distinguishes 'For a Producer on their own work' from 'For everyone else'. 02.01.02's reconciliation explicitly corrected 02.05 and 02.03.03 but left 02.01.01's ledger scope untouched.
findings.forcedInvention: Whether a non-participant viewing a work's credit ledger sees a contested badge. One reading publishes pendency to the public (the harm 02.01.02 DT-05 calls 'the most consequential finding in this pass'); the other hides it. No marker, owner or deferral covers the discrepancy.

findings.claim: 02.01.03 D-04's density floor is defined over 'attested-tier-or-higher' nodes, a tier name that does not exist in 02.04.02's ratified six-rung ladder. The rung the floor counts from is not determinable from the corpus.
findings.evidence: 02.01.03-credit-search-graph-traversal.md:87 (D-04) — 'Density floor for co-contribution: disabled when the query's constraint scope ... has < 20 reachable attested-tier-or-higher nodes; degraded (low-confidence banner) at 20–99; normal at ≥ 100. Self-asserted-tier edges do not count toward the floor.' The authoritative ladder at 02.04.02-provenance-tiers-credit-confidence.md:46-53 names the six rungs 'Imported', 'Self-asserted', 'Asserted by the session owner', 'Session-logged', 'Confirmed', 'Captured and confirmed' — none is called 'attested'. Elsewhere the corpus maps its tier language onto rung numbers explicitly (02.04-attestation-credit-confidence-index.md:47 — "02.08's low-tier RIN exclusion is unreachable by demotion (it fires on rungs 1–2)"), so the omission here is not a convention.
findings.forcedInvention: Whether the floor counts rung ≥ 4 ('Session-logged', platform-observed but unconfirmed) or rung ≥ 5 ('Confirmed', independently attested). The choice decides whether co-contribution search is switched off in a given region/role scope, which is a user-visible product behaviour, and the two readings give materially different node counts in a young graph.

findings.claim: 02.01.04 promises unmerge for 'a bounded window' without stating the bound, and its open question explicitly covers only a different half of the problem.
findings.evidence: 02.01.04-identifier-resolution-duplicate-merge.md:47 (edge case, 'Wrong merge confirmed') — 'Unmerge exists as a first-class inverse ... | "Undo this merge" available for a bounded window; on undo, both discographies reappear as they were pre-merge'. The file's Q-01 (02.01.04-identifier-resolution-duplicate-merge.md:90) narrows itself to the other half — 'Still open: clean restoration after subsequent edits to the merged node' — and D-01/D-02/D-03 say nothing about duration. By contrast the domain sets explicit windows everywhere else it makes this shape of promise (02.01.05 D-13 '7 days', D-11 '72-hour objection window'; 02.02.01 D-12 'reversible within 24h'), so the omission is not house style.
findings.forcedInvention: The length of the unmerge window — 24 hours, 30 days, or indefinite. It determines whether a victim of a wrong person-merge (which D-01 calls 'asymmetric, potentially irreversible, financially consequential harm' and which 'the victim may not notice for years' per DT-01) has any self-service recovery path at all.

findings.claim: The sub-domain CX file still records the sequential wrap→reconcile→prompt→confirmations chain that 02.02.03 D-05 and DT-04 explicitly reject and call the design's central error. The reconciliation was flagged rather than made, and the flag names a workflow step that has already run.
findings.evidence: 02.02-session-capture-cx.md:56 (CX-02 synthesis Q2) — 'Trigger chain: Wrap signal → reconcile → prompt → per-row confirmations → credit records.' Contradicted by 02.02.03-session-close-capture-prompt.md:206 (D-05) — 'The contributor asks and the Producer's reconciliation are two independently-firing halves. Both fire within 5 s of the wrap signal; neither gates the other', and by the same file's DT-04 at line 170 — 'REJECTED — this was the design's central error, and it inverted its own thesis. It gates the perishable asset on the durable one.' 02.02.03 itself records that the fix was never applied: 02.02.03-session-close-capture-prompt.md:185 — 'Step 6 must reconcile CX-02's trigger chain against D-05: CX-02 records "wrap → reconcile → prompt → confirmations", which is the sequential model DT-04 rejects ... This is a change to a sibling artifact I do not own, flagged rather than made.' The tracking is malformed: it names no owner and defers to 'Step 6' of a discovery pass the sibling CX files record as complete (credits-attribution-cx.md:5 — 'Status: [DEEP] — children deepened (Step 5); intra-domain cross-cuts synthesised').
findings.forcedInvention: Whether contributor confirmation cards are dispatched at wrap independently of the Producer's review, or wait behind it. This is the difference between capturing the in-room tap and losing it, and it is the sub-domain's stated highest-value behaviour.

findings.claim: 02.02.02 D-12 makes `never publish` a value set on a contribution at capture — where the Producer is the capture actor for other people's rows — while 02.01.05 makes the permanent-suppression level bilateral and leaves its existence an open owner question. Who may impose permanent non-publication on another party's contribution is unspecified.
findings.evidence: 02.02.02-per-track-contribution-log.md:194 (D-12) — 'A contribution carries visibility intent at capture, including `never publish` | DT-07. Ghost production is permanent, not embargoed.' 02.01.05, named as the feature that honours the intent (02.02.02-per-track-contribution-log.md:76 — 'and 02.01.05 is where the intent is honoured'), makes the corresponding level bilateral: 02.01.05-credit-visibility-embargo.md:39 (Axis A table) — 'Confidential | Per credit, permanent | The credited party + the work's ledger owner | Never, unless both parties agree to lift', and 02.01.05-credit-visibility-embargo.md:181 — 'Axis A's `Confidential` level is where it lands — per credit, permanent, requiring the assent of both the credited party and the work's ledger owner'. Its existence is not settled: 02.01.05-credit-visibility-embargo.md:293 (Q-02b) — 'should WeJammin support `Confidential` (permanent, contractual non-credit) at all, given ghost production is endemic?' — owner-held, deferred to /create-prd. Meanwhile credits-attribution-cx.md:46 (CX-01) states the requirement flatly with no marker: '02.01.05 ... must therefore hold two kinds of suppression (time-bound embargo and unbounded ghosting) or the ghost producer cannot use the log at all.'
findings.forcedInvention: Whether a Producer setting `never publish` on a contribution row naming another party takes effect unilaterally at capture, or is only a request pending that party's assent; and whether the value exists in v1 at all given 02.01.05 Q-02(b).

findings.claim: 02.02.01 D-09 scopes a Musician's roll visibility to overlapping presence intervals specifically to stop an async contributor learning an unreleased record's personnel, while 02.01.05 DT-13 explicitly rejects interval-scoped participant visibility and grants every participant the session's credits — which are the personnel.
findings.evidence: 02.02.01-session-roll-call.md:216 (D-09) — 'A Musician sees only the roll entries whose intervals overlap their own, plus the session owner', justified at line 178 (DT-10) — 'What it prevents is real: an asynchronous contributor who emailed one part learning the full unreleased personnel of a record, weeks before announcement'. Directly opposed at 02.01.05-credit-visibility-embargo.md:115 — 'Explicitly rejected: scoping a participant's visibility to the intervals they attended (DT-13). A dep who played 2pm–3pm sees the session's credits, not a 60-minute slice — an NDA covers the project, not your hours', with D-14 at line 278 making participant status 'per session, binary, and permanent'. The async contributor is inside that participant set: 02.01.05-credit-visibility-embargo.md:113 — 'The participant set is the session roll (02.02.01) — every party on it', and 02.02.01-session-roll-call.md:124 makes the async contributor a roll entry ('Roll entry marked `remote — asynchronous`').
findings.forcedInvention: Whether the participant read of embargoed credits is itself interval-filtered. Implemented literally, both rules ship and D-09's stated protection is void (the async contributor reads the personnel off the credits instead of the roll); implemented consistently, one of two ratified decisions must be overridden.

findings.claim: 02.02.04's highest-stakes edge case leaves its user-facing behaviour as a `[PENDING — Step 5]` marker with no owner and a deferral target that is a discovery step already completed.
findings.evidence: 02.02.04-session-attendance-proof.md:49 — 'Everyone co-signs a fabricated session | The attack. Corroboration is only as honest as the corroborators — five colluding people produce a fully corroborated fake session ... | `[PENDING — Step 5]`'. The row's own What Happens column was revised in this pass (it cites 02.04.02 D-19 and 02.04.04 D-08, both dated ratifications, and the file header reads 'Last updated: 2026-07-23'), so Step 5 has demonstrably run and the marker was left behind. Every other open item in this unit carries a named owner and a pipeline stage (e.g. 02.02.04-session-attendance-proof.md:93 — 'Q-01 | [OWNER] Is device/location presence in scope at all ... | User | /create-prd'), so this is a defective marker rather than the file's convention.
findings.forcedInvention: What a user is shown when a fully co-signed session is a fabrication. The adjacent decisions settle the internal effect (score-only demotion) and explicitly state the accepted cost, but the User Sees cell is the only one in the table with no answer.

findings.claim: 02.03.03 leaves the unwinding of a years-late claim contest as a `[PENDING — Step 5]` marker with no owner and a completed-stage target, even though the row names concrete downstream effects that must be reversed.
findings.evidence: 02.03.03-claim-adjudication.md:69 — 'Claim contested years after attachment | Same path; the credit has by then accumulated downstream effects (royalty registration, reputation, traversal edges) that must unwind | `[PENDING — Step 5]`'. Step 5 has run on this file — its D-05 and D-06 are recorded as 'Owner ratification of DQ-04.1' / 'DQ-04.2' (02.03.03-claim-adjudication.md:107-108) and the header reads 'Last updated: 2026-07-23'. The file's other gaps are properly tracked with owner and stage (e.g. 02.03.03-claim-adjudication.md:118 — 'Q-05 | Pendency is unbounded in the worst case ... | User | /create-prd'), and the parallel unwind question is owned elsewhere for retraction (02.04.03-attestation-retraction.md:91 Q-03, resolved to domain 10) — so no owner has been assigned to the claim-contest case.
findings.forcedInvention: What happens to a filed royalty registration, accumulated traversal edges and reputation effects when a credit detaches from a claimant years after attachment — and which domain owns the reversal.

findings.claim: The rung ladder is defined as purely kind-gated with no rung-order preconditions, so rung 5's gate ('one independent co-present confirmation') is satisfiable by an imported credit — while three other statements say an import is permanently capped at rung 1 and can rise only through fresh capture. The ceiling rule on the domain's central model is not determinable.
findings.evidence: The gate is unconditional on prior rung: 02.04.02-provenance-tiers-credit-confidence.md:52 (rung 5) — 'Confirmed | ≥1 co-present party, who is neither the asserter nor the credited party, confirmed the contribution (02.04.01)', with the model asserting at line 38 that 'The score never promotes across a rung ... rung 5 requires a kind of evidence ... that you either have or do not.' Rung 1's only stated ceiling is narrower than that: 02.04.02-provenance-tiers-credit-confidence.md:48 — 'Imported | ... Can never rise by claiming (D-03)', and D-03 at line 199 covers only 'Claiming and self-assertion never raise the rung' — attestation is neither. Against that stand three unqualified caps: 02.04.02-provenance-tiers-credit-confidence.md:110 — 'Credit predates the user's adoption | Capped below rung 6 ... Same reason import caps at rung 1'; 02.03-claiming-cold-start-seeding-index.md:38 (D-01) — 'Imported credits can never reach the tier that captured credits reach'; and 02.03.01-external-catalog-import.md:47 — 'It stays pinned at import tier and can never be promoted on the strength of that dead source — only a fresh capture (sub-domain D-01) can raise it'. credits-attribution-cx.md:93 (CX-03) gives a fourth, different rule: 'A later contemporaneous attestation can exceed the cap only if a real session record appears; otherwise the cap holds.' Nothing in 02.04.01 blocks the request: its context floor (D-14, line 254) needs only 'work + date + ≥1 other named party present', all of which a Discogs/MusicBrainz import routinely carries.
findings.forcedInvention: Whether an independent co-present party's confirmation lifts an imported credit off rung 1, and if it does not, which mechanism blocks it — an explicit rung-1 lock, an origin precondition on rungs 4–6, or an addressable-set rule that refuses attestation requests on import-origin credits. The choice decides whether a 1994 catalogue credit confirmed by the producer who was actually there renders as 'Confirmed by 1 person who was there' or stays 'Listed on Discogs', and it is the exact laundering boundary 02.03 D-01 calls 'the distinction is the product'.
